description: A land trust holding 145 acres in southern Oregon, welcoming all women and children to live, camp, or relax.
raw_text: LAND TRUSTS FOR WOMEN is an effort to give women control over their own destinies. Two groups of women have researched the concept of land trusts, and formed groups to acquire land for all women and children at all times. This would promote the spiritual, emotional, physical, cultural, and economic well-being of women, and preserve the land. Many of us love nature deeply, and need to live with green all around us and be self-sufficient. We feel caged in polluted, violent cities where we survive day to day by doing meaningless work or by standing in welfare lines. Financially poor women are unable to buy rural property. Private ownership creates hassles anyway. Putting land in a land trust removes it from the speculative market. It would be available to all women and children, whether they want to live there or just stop for a short time, camp out, and relax. We can help women set up local land trusts, or they can join us. Oregon Women's Land Trust has bought 145 acres in southern Oregon. Write OWLT, Box 1713, Eugene, OR, 97401, or California Women's Land Trust, c/o Carole & Yolanda, 1538 N. St. Andrews, Hollywood, CA, 90028.
notes: Type is Land Trust because listing says 'Putting land in a land trust' and mentions 'Oregon Women's Land Trust has bought 145 acres'. Accepted groups: 'all women and children' gives Lesbian women, Non-lesbian women, Girl children, Boy children under pre-1986 rules.

description: An intentional community on 80 acres in northwest Arkansas, practicing lesbian separatism and focusing on farming.
raw_text: WOMEN ON LAND has "secured" 80 acres of land in northwest Arkansas as a beginning for a women's land trust. We are investigating and researching the details of how to form a land trust. We believe a land trust is a way each woman involved with this land can have equal access and responsibility to the land to the feminist community. The concept of a land trust can take care of legal trips and power trips. The land can be legally "owned" by the land trust and each woman could have lease for lifetime use of the land. There is much to be worked out, but we want to know that no woman woman will get ripped off after putting in her time, energy, work, or money. It is difficult to review all the research and energy into laws, qualifying to fit their rules, and at the same time, trying to build a new culture, but we have to use their laws for some measure of protection against them. We will live only with dykes. We wish to relate to female children only - male children would be too sexist an influence on a developing women's environment. We want to stress farming on this land to raise food to feed the women on the land and support sisters in the cities. There are no buildings on the land, just 80 acres of beautiful trees, a waterfall, a creek, and lots of painful bugs. We need to share the responsibility for getting money to pay off the land, for gathering tools, building materials, seed, horse, windmill. We are open to any woman who wants to relate to this land whether she wants to stay full-time, work for the summer, camp and work, spend the weekend, or stay here on the way cross country. We do want to emphasize the need to work. When you write, describe yourself, your politics, what you can offer and why you want to come. (No dogs please.) Send a stamped, self-addressed envelope to Women on Land, PO Box 521, Fayetteville, Arkansas, 72701.
notes: Type is Intentional Community/Cooperative because women are establishing a residential community. Accepted groups: 'live only with dykes' and 'female children only' gives Lesbian women and Girl children. Focuses: 'We will live only with dykes' gives Lesbian separatism; 'stress farming on this land' gives Farming/self-sufficiency.

raw_text: SAPPHA SURVIVAL SCHOOL is a small lesbian farm in the eastern foothills of the Cascade mountains in Washington. One woman who stayed there for a week last summer wrote the following about SSS. "Two women and one child, with many visitors, started this spring to rebuild an old farm valley into a place for all women to work and live, or visit. I helped rebuild the old cabin, later to be the community center, helped dig a well, and build a chicken coop. Freedom and Dykepride run strong - the valley is isolated enough to remove society's inhibitions and its censure of lesbians. Olivia Newton Outhouse is presently open to the sky and a valley view, stream water is pumped to flow between pine branches for the shower and half naked Amazons are everywhere! Evening relaxation is often a sauna, fueled by hot rocks and followed by a dip in the stream." This summer they planned on more structures including a children's space scaled to their size, and an outrageous playground scaled to everybody's size. They also planned an herb garden, a festival in June, and workshops on health. To find out more, write: SSS, Box 4D, Aeneaes Valley Road, Tonasket, WA, 98855.

raw_text: WOMANSHARE is a feminist country retreat. It is run by a collective of five women who open their house for workshops to women seeking more about themselves and their lives. They say, "we feel that living with each other in the country has helped us to become stronger, healthier, more centered, and more creative. Some of the things we have been dealing with are our feminist politics, our sexuality and our own creativity. We know that we need contact with other women and we also need to find a way to survive economically in the country. Womanshare is our way of doing this." It is a special place where women may come together away from the daily hassles of the patriarchal society and experience the strength of a woman's culture. It is not a resort. Each woman who comes to the land makes a commitment to herself and other women thereby accepting responsibility for herself, as well as by respecting and supporting other sisters who are there.
